name: A thermocycler program
description: one named program as it is loaded on the lab's thermocyclers — its steps, their temperatures and durations, and what it is for; the thing a construction file or labsheet means when it says "run GG1"
phrases: the shape of a thermocycler program
what is the gibson thermocycler setting

name.description: the name as it is loaded on the machine and as a labsheet writes it, case-sensitive. The PrimeSTAR GXL family encodes its own parameters — PG<size>K<anneal>, so PG6K55 is a 6 kb target at 55 C annealing with extension at 1 min/kb — and a name of that shape that does not match its steps is an error rather than a nickname.

steps.description: the program in order. NULL means the conditions are not recorded, which is NOT the same as a program with no steps: `incomplete` must then be true and the caller must refuse to compute a duration.

target_kb.description: the product size the program was built for. Advisory: the machine does not enforce it, and a program run on a longer target simply fails.

incomplete.description: TRUE WHEN THE LAB RUNS THIS PROGRAM AND NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN WHAT IT DOES. It is not a draft and not a deprecation — it is a program in active use whose definition is missing, which is a different and more urgent thing than a program that does not exist. GIB2 is named by three issued labpackets and defined nowhere.

unknown.description: which parts are missing, named one by one. 'the duration of the 50 C hold' tells somebody what to go and measure; a bare `incomplete: true` does not.

source.description: where the conditions were transcribed from, so a reader can check them rather than trust them. The PGXL programs come from Pimar issue #22.

time_s.description: seconds. ZERO MEANS AN INFINITE HOLD — the terminal 16 C that runs until somebody opens the lid — and NULL means the duration is unrecorded. These are opposite findings and must never be collapsed: a scheduler that reads null as 0 promises a slot for a run whose length nobody knows.

notes: WHY THIS SCHEMA EXISTS. On 2026-10-14 a student asked which thermocycler program to use for a Gibson, because the machine had no Gibson setting. The program GIB2 was named on three issued labpackets and its conditions were recorded nowhere — not in the labsheets, not in the tutorials, not in this repository. Meanwhile GG1 existed in three places at once, one of which `protocols/modules/golden_gate_assembly.js` already flagged as wrong. A program is an object the lab runs, and it needed one home and one shape.
